original_question: Does there exist a Banach algebra A that is approximately amenable, meaning that every continuous derivation D: A -> X* into the dual of any Banach A-bimodule X is approximately inner, but is not boundedly approximately amenable, meaning that one cannot choose the approximating inner derivations so that they form a bounded net of operators from A into X*?
target_in_paper: Question 1 (first sentence): "Is there an approximately amenable Banach algebra which is not boundedly approximately amenable?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s target as an existence question asking whether approximate amenability can be strictly weaker than bounded approximate amenability. It also correctly spells out approximate amenability via continuous derivations into dual Banach A-bimodules and correctly captures the bounded version as requiring a bounded approximating net of inner derivations.
missing_details: The paper states this as a pure existence question; the nearest official formulation is the first sentence of Question 1, not a broader reformulation involving other neighboring notions.
The ambient setting is a Banach algebra over the complex field.
For bounded approximate amenability, the boundedness is with respect to the approximating inner derivations viewed as operators A -> X*, and the bound may depend on the derivation D.
The official question imposes no extra hypotheses such as unitality, commutativity, separability, or the existence of an approximate identity.
To make the statement fully self-contained, one should explicitly define inner derivations by a -> a·x - x·a and pointwise convergence by D(a)=lim_i(a·x_i-x_i·a) for each a in A.
The paper’s nearby context shows that questions about two-sided or bounded approximate identities are separate open problems, so they should not be inserted as assumptions into this question.
refined_question: Does there exist a complex Banach algebra A such that A is approximately amenable—meaning that for every Banach A-bimodule X and every continuous derivation D:A -> X*, there exists a net (x_i) in X* with D(a)=lim_i(a·x_i-x_i·a) for every a in A—but A is not boundedly approximately amenable, in the sense that for some Banach A-bimodule X and some continuous derivation D:A -> X*, no approximating net of inner derivations can be chosen uniformly bounded in operator norm as maps A -> X*?
justification: The draft is aiming at the first sentence of Question 1, which asks for a counterexample separating approximate amenability from bounded approximate amenability. It should not be expanded to include the second sentence of Question 1 about bounded approximate contractibility, because that is a different neighboring problem. The surrounding discussion in Section 3.1 makes clear that no bounded-approximate-identity hypothesis belongs in the statement itself: Theorem 3.3 only gives one-sided approximate identities for approximately amenable algebras, and Question 4 separately asks whether every approximately amenable Banach algebra must have a two-sided or bounded approximate identity. So the sharp paper-faithful formulation is exactly the existence of an approximately amenable but not boundedly approximately amenable Banach algebra, with the definitions made explicit and no extra assumptions added.
